desc: Ideation: model as functional graph of global renames; consistency of f is the first obstruction.

Prove buffer lemma and exact rules: inconsistent f → -1; infeasible only when T uses all 26 letters and changes are required (f is then a permutation and any first merge is fatal); otherwise minimum = (#letters a with f(a)≠a) + (#isolated cycles, i.e. cycles where every vertex has indegree 1). Cycles with incoming tree edges need no extra op (verified: abc→bcb in 3 ops).
Validate rules against all four samples mentally (4, 0, -1, 4 all reproduced).
Implement full Python solution: parse input, consistency check, build edges, cycle detection on 26-node functional graph, apply feasibility/cost rule, print answer. Complexity O(N + 26).

Verify edge cases: S==T → 0 (edge_count=0, all-26 check guarded by edge_count>0); all-26 permutation with nontrivial cycle → -1; S uses all 26 but T uses fewer → f non-injective, a valid merge x→y with f(x)=f(y) frees a buffer while counting as x's required edge, formula holds; T uses <26 and f injective → S uses <26, initially absent buffer exists; self-maps cost 0 but remain valid targets; isolated-cycle resolution via buffer costs k+1 with standard schedule.
Drop brute-force BFS verification (constructive schedule argument is airtight).
